title: Divergence of humans and chimpanzees
summary: DNA evidence shows that our species and chimpanzees diverged from a common ancestor that lived between 8 and 6 million years ago, according to the Smithsonian. A study using generation times in wild chimpanzees and gorillas puts the split at at least 7 to 8 million years. The difference between the human and chimpanzee genomes in the aspects studied is about 1.2%.

uncertainty.note: Genomic estimates based on ape generation times and mutation rates place the lineage split at least 7–8 million years ago, while fossil discoveries such as Sahelanthropus tchadensis date to between 7 and 6 million years ago.

where.historical_name: Central Africa (late Miocene paleoenvironment; no polities exist)

importance.justification: The separation of the hominin lineage from the common ancestor shared with chimpanzees initiated the evolutionary history of all hominin species, culminating in modern humanity.

related.because: The divergence of the hominin lineage from chimpanzees was the foundational split that led to early Homo sapiens.
